423:449. **When are the nine differences between the two paths that climb batch 29's record did not plan repaired?** Item 76 of PLAN's "Pavol's answers"; finding 4 of climb batch 29's post-batch review. His aim of 15:0x, "bring the two implementations to do the same thing", is met where both paths can show it today. Nine differences that the record did not plan stand, each with its row: 957, 958, 961 and 968, 962, 963, 966, 967, 362 and 446 (`reviews/batch-29-review.md`, section 7). Rows 957, 961 and 968 go with the rebuild of the static numerals on both paths before the switch-over (P-174, P-176; P-37's exception for the numerals, his word of 17:14 UTC on 2026-11-09), so the question stands for the other seven. The question touches phase 4's order, which puts the natives' remainder and then the names batch next.
642:450. **Which class holds the field of a numeral's place at a program's own type (P-176): the component's class, and, at a type that names a type parameter of its generic declaration, the instantiated class?** F.worker.1 and F.skeptic.1 of climb batch 29's rung F. The code generator sets a static field for each numeral site at a program's type in the component class's static initializer, whatever class holds the site (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:7189`, `numeralCoercionSiteDesc`). A site at a program's own generic type is not hoisted, so its coercion runs at each evaluation: two calls of `site(): Gen[\String\] = 3` give two objects (row 957). P-176 answers the generic half: a numeral at a place is one value, made once, at a program's generic type too, so row 957 goes with the rebuild of the static numerals (row 970).
845:462. **A numeral as a `typecase`'s selector keeps `IntLiteral` on the compiled path (rows 963 and 964).** C.skeptic.4 of climb batch 29's rung C. P-173 gives such a numeral its default. The default there moves `compiler_tests/XXX5r.test`'s pinned span, and it makes `XXXPatternMatchingc.test`'s `typecase (3, 4) of (x, y: ZZ32)` reachable, which then stops the code generator (row 964).
594:470. **How is the library's `=/=` over `Any` repaired, so that it answers `NOT (e = e')` at a numeral operand (row 966)?** T.worker.1, T.skeptic.1 and T.judge.2 of climb batch 29's rung T. The library's `=/=` over `Any` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:98`) answers `true` for `u =/= 0` with a zero `u` of `NN32`, `NN64` or `RR32`, and for `q =/= 0.5` with `q: QQ = 1/2`, while `u = 0` and `q = 0.5` are `true` through the `=` pairs. The judge upheld this as a departure from `e =/= e'` being `NOT (e = e')`. An `=/=` on each number type as `NOT (self = other)` is not chosen for a numeral operand while the one over `Any` stands.
1095:475. **Rung N's forks N2 and N5 to N12 of climb batch 29, taken at their defaults, with N7's departure.** The record's forks 10 and 13 to 20: the checker's names switch by library, as `CHARACTER` does (N2); one rounding by a new pair of helpers that both paths call (N5); walk's choice of a declaration reads a numeral argument as the checker does (N6); where walk converts a numeral, and how (N7); the `=` pairs kept and completed, 11 coercions with their pairs (N8); the `SEQV` of two numeral objects inside a coercion's body by their reduced values (N9); a numeral object printed as the Working Draft writes a numeral (N10); walk's glue classes of the two objects kept, unused, until the names batch's clean-up (N11); the tests whose answer the design drops, promoted or removed (N12). N7 departs: walk converts by the library's own coercion, not by walk's Java (item 456). N1, N3 and N4 are items 476 to 478. The static numerals answer N7 to N10 (P-174, P-176): no numeral value exists when a program runs, so no `=` pairs, no `SEQV` of numeral objects and no printing of one, and walk converts through the coercion instantiated with the four numbers (items 456, 476 and 478, in (a)); the landed forks go with row 969.
460:477. **Fork N3: `Numeral` below `Number`, the getters' half answered.** The record's fork 11; consequential by the Fable review of the record, where the record lists it routine. The static numerals give a numeral type no getters (P-174), so the getters' half has no object; the landed getters go with row 969. They are `digits`, `fractionDigits`, `radix` and `digitValue`, the names that the prototype proposed: `ZZ32` for the first three, and `ZZ` for the value, which a 20-digit numeral needs. `Numeral` extends `Number`, as `IntLiteral` did, so the library's `excludes` clauses and P-160's Meet Rule readings stand with the names changed.
1102:479. **Rung C's forks C1 to C3 and C5 to C8 of climb batch 29, taken at their defaults, with C6 not built.** The record's forks 21 to 23 and 25 to 28: the default applies exactly at P-173's places that fix no type (C1); the written-only rule reads written types, so `t = x` inside a coercion's body binds `t` at the numeral type (C2; item 443); a numeral outside its type's range, or whose one rounding is an infinity, is refused statically (C3; rows 325 and 967); a size read as a value is a `ZZ32` (C5; row 486); a negative constant at a program's type is prefix `-` on its coercion of the natural numeral (C6); the tests of rows 362 and 506 promoted or rewritten (C7); `InferO2Pos.fss:18-19` respelled to P-173's answer (C8). C6 is not built, and the landed tree departs from it (item 448). C4 is item 480.
